metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >50% negative values in recent 7–10 days), model tends to over-forecast upward; correct by reducing forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day average), model often overshoots; apply a 3–5 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 5–10% from peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days unless confirmed by event-driven catalyst.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early dip (e.g., first 3–5 days below 30-day MA), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% for first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to over-forecast recovery; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days.
